chunks: Sa'd narrated from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subbah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who stands in the prayer row alone, so he said: 'There is no harm in it; they merely appear one after another.'

key_terms.الصَّفِّ: The row or line in congregational prayer
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible
key_terms.يَبْدُو: To appear or become visible (referring to the row filling up)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to stand alone in a prayer row during congregational prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the permissibility of a lone individual remaining in a prayer row (*saff*) rather than moving to the front, emphasizing the natural progression of the congregation. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the physical arrangement of prayer, prioritizing the continuity of the collective act over rigid positional adjustments. It reflects the broader scholarly principle that the validity of the *saff* is maintained as long as the connection is not intentionally broken, accommodating the dynamic nature of communal worship.
